dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Do not escalate or restate revenue on the supplied evidence."
"Keep restatement on hold pending the result."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Reconciling dealer settlement cycles against bank remittance logs confirms that funds arrived in accordance with monthly credit agreements without revenue inflation." No bank remittance-log source, query, or reconciliation result is identified elsewhere in the submission, so this is not reproducibly supported.

"Revenue Manipulation: rejected because all 17 renewals ... correspond to genuine retail transaction dates ... with complete bank cash settlement." The dealer email corroborates the posting convention but does not independently establish that every transaction was genuine or exclude intentional timing manipulation; unique source IDs and ledger reconciliation also do not fully prove absence of manipulation.

"The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates" is presented as a high-confidence aggregate claim without reporting the actual comparison query or row-level exception check.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission considered a pipeline defect, revenue manipulation, recognition-policy mismatch, and entitlement failure. The strongest alternative it only partially handled is intentional period-stuffing or manipulated retention timing using legitimate-looking dealer transactions: the email and reconciliation support a benign posting explanation but are not independent proof against that hypothesis. It also appropriately preserved the possibility of an entitlement or event-time analytics problem.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide a reproducible row-level reconciliation/query output linking each affected recharge to its import record and independent cash/remittance evidence, while explicitly comparing `effective_event_date` and `posted_at` in downstream retention reporting. This would substantiate the cash claim and make the rejection of manipulation and pipeline defect materially stronger.

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Unknown 1 — repeat contact: I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."
"Which exact terminal stages and outcomes are excluded from the containment denominator?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "New self-service stages balance_check (29.1% of sessions) and pack_info (21.3%) do not exist at all under legacy routing (0%), representing genuine deflection for authenticated callers." Stage frequencies and absence under legacy routing do not by themselves establish successful resolution, authentication status, or improved customer experience.

"The 650 pre-authentication drops ... represent uncaptured customer friction rather than successful self-service resolution." The submission does not establish that these sessions were complaints, that they failed rather than ended through an acceptable path, or that they were followed by repeat contact.

"Analysis ... confirms that the apparent drop is an artifact of measurement changes." The evidence strongly supports changed measurement as a plausible explanation, but does not rule out genuine containment or quantify its contribution.

"Telemetry ... confirms ongoing customer impact." Service events show operational incidents and affected accounts, but do not directly establish complaint volume, dissatisfaction, or the outcomes of NovaIVR users.

The proposed "7-day repeat contacts across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions" may not be feasible as a subscriber-level reconciliation for pre-authentication sessions that lack verified customer context; the linkage limitation should be tested explicitly.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst partially handled genuine improvement by noting that a low repeat-contact rate would make containment more credible and by identifying new terminal stages, but it missed or underweighted the strongest benign alternative: some authentication-stage or abandoned sessions may be non-complaint interactions that ended acceptably or were not followed by any customer harm. It also did not clearly separate network-event severity from complaint outcomes.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the assertion that pre-authentication sessions are customer friction with an explicit outcome-validation plan: determine which sessions can be linked to subscribers, measure repeat contacts and recovery by journey stage, and sample/listen to unlinked calls to distinguish technical failure, ordinary abandonment, successful resolution, and complaints.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and names the relevant fields for severity, duration, timestamps, inverter IDs, impact, and cleared status.
The claim that all four events had zero impact and were cleared is explicitly tied to `impact_mw` and `cleared`, with the observed counts stated as 0/4 nonzero-impact and 0/4 open records.
It distinguishes the observed event data from the inference that labels alone do not establish failure, and acknowledges that constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst triangulates event severity, duration, inverter identity, cleared status, and generation impact rather than relying only on the warning label.
It tests the plausible innocent explanation that the extract may be incomplete by noting the absence of an unfiltered plant baseline and extraction parameters.
The recommendation to perform a read-only unfiltered query before equipment investigation is consistent with the observed zero-impact, short, cleared events.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission states that constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units and that the four-row extract lacks an unfiltered baseline or extraction parameters.
It avoids claiming that the warning proves equipment failure and conditions escalation on open faults, recurrence, critical severity, or nonzero impact in a broader pull.
The conclusion is appropriately scoped to holding escalation and checking completeness rather than declaring the plant healthy.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: The proposed action is a proportionate, read-only export query for 27 May–4 June without status filters, followed by re-evaluation only if materially different records appear.
The action preserves operational caution while avoiding an unsupported equipment intervention, given four cleared events, zero MW impact, and 13 total minutes.
The stated decision rule—reconsider if the pull reveals recurrence, open status, critical severity, or nonzero impact—is discriminating and linked to the evidence.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion, “Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check,” matches the visible pattern of four short, cleared events across four inverters with zero recorded generation impact.
The submission correctly treats the seven-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` as a low-priority quality/completeness signal rather than evidence of a plant equipment problem.
The proposed stopping point—close the review if the broader pull contains only these four records—is appropriately limited to this review scope.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “These observations provide zero escalation signal” is somewhat too absolute: they provide little direct equipment-escalation signal, but the warning and incomplete extract provide a limited data-quality signal.
“This query is completely safe and reversible” is reasonable for a read-only query but unnecessarily absolute; query permissions, scope, and system load are not documented.
Removing status filters alone may not establish completeness if other filters, unit scope, pagination, timezone handling, or export limitations remain unspecified.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The seven-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` could represent a transient communications-path issue rather than an inverter or generation problem; alternatively, the extract may be incomplete and conceal recurrence or open/nonzero-impact events. The submission appropriately treats both as possibilities requiring only a completeness check, not as established mechanisms.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the cheap check explicitly plant-wide and unfiltered across all relevant dimensions, while verifying date/timezone boundaries, pagination, and export metadata; this would test completeness more decisively than merely removing status filters.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “Recomputing from `dispatch_blocks.csv` reproduces the headline cross-day arithmetic exactly” with specified daily penalty totals and calculation.
“On 29 May, 84 blocks retain `qca_base` and 12 are `pilot_revision`,” using `base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, and `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`.
The submission explicitly distinguishes the observed 28-to-29 May difference from the inferred same-day modeled counterfactual and identifies missing settlement and timestamp evidence.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: “Credit the arithmetic, reject the attribution” correctly notices that the 31.6% result compares different days.
The analyst constructs the required same-day comparison: base schedule versus submitted schedule on 29 May against the same actual generation.

The submission tests multiple alternatives, including arithmetic fabrication, metric definition, forecast skill versus hindsight, and net commercial value, rather than treating the headline as causal proof.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “This within-day association does not establish general causal efficacy.”
“High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation” appropriately separates computational confidence from causal confidence.
The analyst identifies specific decision-changing evidence: immutable pre-submission timestamps and complete net-settlement modeling.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold expansion” follows from the limited one-day evidence without treating the pilot as worthless.
The recommendation for a “read-only shadow calculation” preserves operational and source-record safety.
The proposed next measurement—pre-registered matched high-wind days, immutable timestamps, base-versus-submitted shadow calculations, and net commercial value—is discriminating rather than generic.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “The defensible within-day figure is ~17.6%, not 31.6%” accurately preserves the smaller same-day benefit while rejecting unsupported causal attribution.
“Report 31.6% only as the descriptive 28-to-29 May difference and 17.6% only as the modeled one-day estimate” is appropriately scoped.
The conclusion matches the evidence: pilot-day performance improved relative to the modeled base schedule, but neither result establishes a general causal commercial effect.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Observed: the 28-to-29 May penalty arithmetic and the same-day base-versus-submitted calculation, as described from `dispatch_blocks.csv`.
Inferred: “achieved a modeled penalty approximately 17.6% lower” is valid as a modeled within-day association, but should not be read as an operationally realized causal saving.

Slightly overstated: “post-hoc adjustments invalidate the AI claim” is too absolute; they would invalidate or weaken a claim of pre-generation predictive skill, but could still show post-hoc operational performance.

Unsupported if not directly present in the cited extract: the characterization that the 28 and 29 May wind fields are “similar” should be checked against the actual field values, though it is not central to the conclusion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% reduction could partly reflect different wind or operating conditions between 28 and 29 May, while the 17.6% same-day modeled reduction could still be confounded by schedule-selection or hindsight effects. The evidence supports a promising pilot-day association, not a proven causal reduction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Prioritize an immutable audit of forecast, revision, and submission timestamps for the 12 pilot-revised blocks, then repeat the pre-registered base-versus-submitted comparison across several matched high-wind days with full net-settlement modeling.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No record contradicts 90211000" is an absence claim that is not independently demonstrated beyond the listed records.

"This is ... the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence" is somewhat overstated; the submission also identifies an unresolved invoice-value presentation issue and does not establish whether the cited matrix entry was legally effective on the shipment date.
"Different code escalates; 90211000 closes the flag" assumes the requested Tares or ruling is decisive without specifying how conflicting or nonbinding evidence would be handled.

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The mismatch could still reflect a stale or incorrectly applied Swiss matrix entry, a shipment-date/version mismatch, or an erroneous declaration; 90211090 could be the applicable Swiss code on 2025-11-04. Tares or an authoritative ruling effective for that date is therefore necessary before final closure.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote the relevant Swiss matrix/Tares provisions and verify the effective jurisdiction, version, and date for 2025-11-04, including how conflicting or nonbinding results would affect escalation.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim."
"without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is stated categorically; the evidence establishes that such support is missing from the reviewed packet, but does not by itself establish that an active linked supplier declaration is the only legally sufficient form of proof.

"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral)" is not fully supported because the submission does not establish the applicable non-preferential tariff treatment or demonstrate that 0.0% duty is neutral under that treatment.

The statement that valid EU supplier declarations "exist for other suppliers" appears to rely on register entries, but the submission does not establish that those entries are shipment-specific declarations or that the listed suppliers supplied P1006 in this shipment.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been supplied by SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or a valid declaration may exist in Procurement's archives; the missing packet linkage may therefore be a documentation or data-lineage failure rather than an invalid preference claim. Conversely, if no qualifying declaration covers 2025-09-18, the claim should be corrected or removed, but the available evidence still does not establish fraud.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Verify the shipment-to-supplier link and obtain the supplier's dated declaration and applicable preferential-origin rule before directing non-preferential treatment, while preserving the reversible administrative hold.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Read-only live audit of 10 batches with 02:10:00 extract timestamps"
"obtaining verified upload timestamps would resolve the true start of the release clock before building any report"
"Survival tracking of the 42 currently open HOLD rows"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not supported by the submission's own statement that `evidence_available_ts` is absent; it appears to relabel a proxy as evidence-to-release.

"the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" is directionally plausible and strongly suggested by the snapshot-time match, but should remain an inference until event-level or live-record timestamps are compared.

The proposed evidence check focuses on certificate upload times, but the SOP clock depends on all required evidence, including specifications and deviation information, so certificate timestamps alone may not establish `evidence_available_ts`.

The claim that completed-only estimates are biased downward is plausible given right-censoring, but the magnitude and direction of overall queue-health bias require final outcomes or a survival analysis.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration could be a mixture of genuine releases and interface batching rather than a pure synchronization artifact; receipt-to-release delay may therefore include both real workflow delay and timestamp/interface delay. The data supports deferring KPI publication, but not yet quantifying how much of the 45.5-hour mean is measurement artifact versus operational queue time.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the unsupported 8.4-hour "evidence-to-release" result with an explicitly labeled proxy, and obtain an event-level audit for a small stratified sample of default-timestamp and non-default batches showing availability of every required evidence type plus the actual disposition decision time; use that comparison to define the KPI before reporting performance.

"What Would Change the Decision" maps identity, current stock, revision approval, and search-value evidence to concrete decision changes.

The submission identifies what future evidence could revive its conclusions, but does not fully test the competing explanation that semantic search may recover useful matches among the 11 requests lacking MPNs.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records" — requests targeted identity evidence for blank-part-number requests.
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query" — directly addresses the highest operational risk from stale or negative availability.
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search" — proposes a discriminating evaluation, though the evidence requests are not explicitly ranked by expected decision impact.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "semantic search is not the real problem" is too strong: exact matching all 13 populated-MPN requests does not test whether semantic search can recover candidates for the 11 requests lacking identifiers.

"the firm saving is $20.5k" is not established by quoted external prices and stale global inventory; it is better characterized as potential candidate value subject to live confirmation and transfer costs.
The eight items labeled "Actionable now" remain conditional because the cited global stock snapshot is older than the request export and current reservations or movements are not fully confirmed.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching may show that search is adequate for identified requests while semantic search remains valuable for the 11 requests without MPNs; the dominant constraint may be a combination of identifier quality and retrieval, not data hygiene alone. In addition, stale extracts may make the apparent actionable/restricted split a temporal artifact.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a controlled, row-level validation of the 11 blank-MPN requests plus the eight proposed actionable transfers using current local CMMS availability, reservation, revision, UOM, and qualification data; compare exact-match and semantic-search recall and precision on that same validated set before claiming savings or deprioritizing semantic search.
